entries.description:
The configuration's global names — the entry points a module reaches its objects through: Constants, Catalogs, Documents, Enumerations, DataProcessors and Reports with their external counterparts, the registers and the charts, Sequences, SessionParameters, FunctionalOptions, ScheduledJobs and BackgroundJobs. Each is written without a prefix and made when it is read, so it always reflects the configuration as it is. The object itself is never named in a script.

ScheduledJobs and BackgroundJobs have articles of their own, under Scheduled and background jobs. Beside these names stand Metadata — the configuration's description — and Data — its data sources for LINQ.
The constants of the configuration, by name. `Constants.<Name>` is the constant's manager: Get() reads the value kept in the base, Set(value) writes it. Read-only itself — a ManagerCollection.

The catalogs of the configuration, by name. `Catalogs.<Name>` is the catalog's manager: CreateItem, CreateFolder, FindByCode, FindByDescription, Select, EmptyRef, GetForm, GetListForm, GetSelectForm, GetTemplate, and the Public methods of its manager module.

The documents of the configuration, by name. `Documents.<Name>` is the document's manager: CreateDocument, FindByNumber, Select, EmptyRef, GetForm, GetListForm, GetSelectForm, GetTemplate, and the Public methods of its manager module.

The configuration's own enumerations, by name. `Enumerations.<Name>` is the enumeration's manager: its values by name, EmptyRef, and the forms. The platform's enumerations (TextEncoding, SortDirection, …) are global names of their own and are not here.
The data processors of the configuration, by name. `DataProcessors.<Name>` is the processor's manager: Create() makes a new object of it, GetForm and GetTemplate reach its forms and templates.
entries.return_descr: ManagerCollection of the data processors' managers.

entries.description: Data processors kept in files outside the configuration. Create(fullPath) loads one and answers with its object.
The reports of the configuration, by name. `Reports.<Name>` is the report's manager: Create() makes a new object of it, GetForm and GetTemplate reach its forms and templates.
Reports kept in files outside the configuration. Create(fullPath) loads one and answers with its object.

The information registers of the configuration, by name. `InformationRegisters.<Name>` is the register's manager: CreateRecordSet, CreateRecordManager, CreateRecordKey, Get, GetFirst, GetLast, SliceFirst, SliceLast, Select, and the forms.

The accumulation registers of the configuration, by name. `AccumulationRegisters.<Name>` is the register's manager: CreateRecordSet, CreateRecordKey, Balance, Turnovers, Select, and the forms. A document writes the movements through its RegisterRecords.

The charts of characteristic types of the configuration, by name. `ChartsOfCharacteristicTypes.<Name>` is the chart's manager: CreateItem, CreateFolder, FindByCode, FindByDescription, Select, EmptyRef, its predefined items by name, and the forms.

The charts of accounts of the configuration, by name. `ChartsOfAccounts.<Name>` is the chart's manager: CreateAccount, CreateFolder, FindByCode, FindByDescription, Select, EmptyRef, its predefined accounts by name, and the forms.

The accounting registers of the configuration, by name. `AccountingRegisters.<Name>` is the register's manager: CreateRecordSet, CreateRecordKey, Balance, Turnovers, DrCrTurnovers, BalanceAndTurnovers, RecordsWithAccountDimensions, Select, and the forms.

The charts of calculation types of the configuration, by name. `ChartsOfCalculationTypes.<Name>` is the chart's manager: CreateCalculationType, CreateFolder, FindByCode, FindByDescription, Select, EmptyRef, its predefined types by name, and the forms.
The calculation registers of the configuration, by name. `CalculationRegisters.<Name>` is the register's manager: CreateRecordSet, CreateRecordKey, Get, GetBase, Select, and the forms.

The sequences of the configuration, by name. `Sequences.<Name>` is the sequence's manager: GetBorder and SetBorder read and move its border, Restore re-posts what lies past it, CreateRecordSet and Select reach its registrations. Inside a document, Sequences names the document's own registrations instead — a RecordRegister.
The configuration's session parameters — values that exist once per session: set by the session module when the session starts, read everywhere afterwards.

The configuration's functional options, by name — whether a part of the configuration is used in this base. An option is kept as a constant is, so `FunctionalOptions.<Name>` is a constant's manager: Get() answers True or False, Set(value) switches it.

What Catalogs, Documents and every other kind of the global context answer with: the managers of that kind's objects, by name. `Catalogs.Goods` — or `Catalogs["Goods"]`, or `Catalogs.Get("Goods")` — is the Goods catalog's manager, made when it is read; the name is compared without regard to case. Get and [ ] take a position too, from 0; Count counts; Foreach hands out the managers in the configuration's order. Nothing can be added to it or removed from it.
How many objects of the kind have a manager — how many catalogs, documents, … the configuration declares.
The manager at a position, from 0, or the one of a name, compared without regard to case — the same as `[ ]`. A name the kind does not have raises, and so does a position past the last one.
entries.parameters: index — a position from 0; or name — the object's name as a string.

entries.description: The configuration's description, as a script reads it: `Metadata.Catalogs.Goods` is the Goods catalog's metadata object — its properties as the designer shows them (Name, Synonym, Comment, …), not its data. One read-only property per kind of object, each a MetadataCollection to read by name, by position or with Foreach.
The configuration's common modules, as metadata objects.
The configuration's common forms, as metadata objects.
The configuration's common templates, as metadata objects.
The configuration's constants, as metadata objects. Their values are read through Constants.
The configuration's catalogs, as metadata objects. Their data is reached through Catalogs.
The configuration's documents, as metadata objects. Their data is reached through Documents.
The configuration's enumerations, as metadata objects. Their values are read through Enumerations.
The configuration's data processors, as metadata objects.
The configuration's reports, as metadata objects.
The configuration's information registers, as metadata objects.
The configuration's accumulation registers, as metadata objects.
The configuration's charts of characteristic types, as metadata objects.
The configuration's charts of accounts, as metadata objects.
The configuration's accounting registers, as metadata objects.
The configuration's charts of calculation types, as metadata objects.
The configuration's calculation registers, as metadata objects.
The configuration's sequences, as metadata objects.

The metadata objects of one kind, by name — what every property of Metadata answers with. `Metadata.Catalogs.Goods`, `Metadata.Catalogs["Goods"]` and `Metadata.Catalogs.Get("Goods")` are one object; the name is compared without regard to case. Get and [ ] take a position too, from 0; Count counts; Foreach hands out the objects themselves. Read-only.
How many objects of the kind the configuration declares.
The metadata object at a position, from 0, or the one of a name, compared without regard to case — the same as `[ ]`. A name the kind does not have raises, and so does a position past the last one.
entries.parameters: index — a position from 0; or name — the object's name as a string.

entries.description:
The configuration's data sources, for LINQ. `Data.Catalogs.Goods` is the Goods catalog as a Queryable — the same source the query language reads with `FROM Catalog.Goods` — and a chain of verbs on it (Where, OrderBy, Take, Count, Any, First, ToArray, ToTable) becomes one query the server runs, where it can; a verb that cannot be translated falls back to reading the rows and working on them in memory, with the same answer. Reading `Data.Catalogs.Goods` reads nothing.

Only the kinds that hold data are here: constants, catalogs, documents, enumerations, the registers, the charts and sequences. From(table) makes a source of a Table held in memory.

A Table held in memory as a data source: the same verbs as a source of the base, and it can be joined with one — the join is then run by the server, the table carried there for the query. Anything but a Table raises.
The configuration's constants as data sources, by name.
The configuration's catalogs as data sources, by name. A row of a catalog's source is its reference.
The configuration's documents as data sources, by name. A row of a document's source is its reference.
The configuration's enumerations as data sources, by name: their values as rows.
The configuration's information registers as data sources, by name. A register has no reference, so its rows come as structures of its columns.
The configuration's accumulation registers as data sources, by name; rows come as structures of the register's columns.
The configuration's charts of characteristic types as data sources, by name.
The configuration's charts of accounts as data sources, by name.
The configuration's accounting registers as data sources, by name; rows come as structures of the register's columns.
The configuration's charts of calculation types as data sources, by name.
The configuration's calculation registers as data sources, by name; rows come as structures of the register's columns.
The configuration's sequences as data sources, by name: their registrations as rows.

The values that exist once per session: one property per session parameter the configuration declares (under Common), named as declared. They are set by the session module's SetSessionParameters when a session starts — every kind of session, background and scheduled jobs included, after the user is known and before the row-access policies are built — and read everywhere afterwards.

A write anywhere else raises: the policies filter rows by these values, so nothing outside the session module may change them. A value is adjusted to the declared type as it is written. A parameter never set reads as its type's empty value — an empty reference of its kind, so a filter against it lets no rows through. Two sessions hold their own values.

The holder behind one session parameter, through which its value is read from the session and written to it, adjusted to the declared type. Reading `SessionParameters.<Name>` hands back the value itself, never the holder, so a script does not hold one; it is a registered type so that the debugger can name it.

What the name of a common module is at run time: `Common.Entry(…)` calls the Public procedure Entry of the common module Common, and TypeOf(Common) answers ModuleManager. Its members are the module's Public procedures and functions and nothing else. A global common module has no name of its own to write: its Public methods are global names.

A common module's name while the code is being edited in the designer: the same members as ModuleManager — the module's Public methods, read from its text — so that the editor can offer them after the dot. It runs nothing; at run time the name is a ModuleManager.

The configuration's own module at run time, one per session — the root every other name is resolved from: the configuration module's Public variables and methods, Metadata, Data, the common modules and the global context. A script never names it; the debugger shows it as the context of the configuration's module.

What ExternalDataProcessors answers with: the door to data processors kept in files outside the configuration. Create(fullPath) loads one and answers with its object — its attributes, its forms and its module's Public methods, as a data processor of the configuration has.
Loads the external data processor from the file at fullPath and answers with a new object of it. A file that cannot be loaded raises (`Failed to load data processor '…'`).
entries.parameters: fullPath — the full path of the processor's file.

entries.description: What ExternalReports answers with: the door to reports kept in files outside the configuration. Create(fullPath) loads one and answers with its object — its attributes, its forms, its templates and its module's Public methods, as a report of the configuration has.
Loads the external report from the file at fullPath and answers with a new object of it. A file that cannot be loaded raises (`Failed to load report '…'`).
entries.parameters: fullPath — the full path of the report's file.

entries.description: The module context of an external data processor that was loaded: the processor object's attributes and methods together with its module's Public methods — the names in scope inside the processor's own module, which reads the configuration's global names through the configuration's root. A script that loaded the processor holds its object, not this.

The module context of an external report that was loaded: the report object's attributes and methods together with its module's Public methods — the names in scope inside the report's own module, which reads the configuration's global names through the configuration's root. A script that loaded the report holds its object, not this.

A document's register records: its RegisterRecords — and, where the document is registered in sequences, its Sequences. One property per register the document records into, named after the register: a record set already set to this document as its recorder, empty until the posting handler fills it.

Posting writes the sets the handler changed after the handler returns, each replacing this document's movements in its register; a set left untouched is not written. Write() writes them earlier, when a later step must read the movements back.

Writes every record set of the list that was changed since it was last read or written — a set filled, or cleared to take the movements away — each replacing this document's movements in its register. A set not changed is not written, so posting does not write it a second time. A register that refuses (a required field, a lock, a right) raises with its own reason.
entries.example:
RegisterRecords.Stock.Clear();
RegisterRecords.Write();   // the movements are gone before the next step reads the balance

entries.description: The Filter of a register's record set: one property per key the set is selected by — the period and the dimensions of an independent information register; the Recorder of an accumulation register, or of an information register subordinate to a recorder. Each is a RecordSetRegisterKeyDescription with Value, Use and Set(value). The set reads and writes the records the filter selects.
One key of a record set's filter: the value it is compared with (Value) and whether it filters at all (Use). A new set filters by nothing — Use is False on every key.
The value the key is compared with. While Use is False it reads as the key's empty value. Writing it sets the value and turns the key on, as Set does.
entries.return_descr: The key's value, or its empty value.

entries.description: Whether the key filters the set. True after Set or after Value is written. Writing False takes the key out of the filter; writing True puts it in with the key's empty value.
Sets the value the key is compared with and turns the key on — the same as writing Value.
entries.parameters: value — the value of the key.

entries.description: The column descriptions of a register's record set — one per field of the register, with Count() and Find(name), read by position. The platform describes a set's rows with it: in a form, when loading and unloading. A record set has no property that hands it to a script; Unload() answers with a Table whose Columns a script reads.

One column of a record set's description: Name, Types, Caption, Width and Indexing, taken from the register's field. Indexing is always False here and cannot be switched on. Reached by the platform, not by a script — see RecordSetRegisterColumn.

The column descriptions of an object's tabular section — one per attribute of the section, with Count() and Find(name). The platform describes the section's rows with it: in a form, when loading and unloading. A tabular section has no property that hands it to a script; Unload() answers with a Table whose Columns a script reads.

One column of a tabular section's description: Name, Types, Caption, Width and Indexing, taken from the section's attribute. Indexing is always False here and cannot be switched on. Reached by the platform, not by a script — see TabularSectionColumn.
